title: Evisceration and Handling of Red and Rough Offal

lessons.title: Evisceration of small stock carcasses
lessons.html:
What evisceration is

Evisceration means removing the organs from the chest and belly of the carcass. It is done in the clean area. The biggest danger is cutting the stomach or intestines, which spills dung and stomach contents onto the meat.

Before you start

  • Clean protective clothing, clean hands, sterile knife.
  • The rectum must be freed and tied or bagged.
  • The oesophagus (weasand) must be tied.

Steps

  1. Open the belly: make a small cut through the belly wall. Put two fingers inside to lift the wall away from the guts. Cut along the middle line with the blade pointing outwards, between your fingers.
  2. Free the rectum and bladder through the pelvis, if not already done.
  3. Remove the rough offal: pull the intestines and stomachs out together in one piece. Cut the attachments carefully. Do not tear the stomachs.
  4. Open the chest: cut through the diaphragm and, if your plant does so, the breastbone.
  5. Remove the red offal (pluck): heart, lungs, liver, and often the windpipe and throat, in one piece.
  6. Remove the kidneys only if your plant does so; often they stay in the carcass for inspection.
  7. Present for inspection: carcass, head and organs together and matched.

If a gut is cut

Stop. Do not wipe or wash. Tell your supervisor. The contaminated part must be trimmed off with a sterile knife, as the meat inspector directs. Sterilise your knife and wash your hands.

lessons.title: Handling red offal
lessons.html:
What red offal is

Red offal is the edible organs: liver, heart, lungs, kidneys, tongue and spleen. Some of these, especially the liver, kidneys and heart, are sold to butcheries and are valuable.

Inspection first

Red offal must be kept matched to its carcass until the meat inspector has passed it. Hang the pluck on the numbered hook or put it on the matching tray. The inspector cuts and looks at the liver, lungs and heart and their lymph nodes.

  • Passed offal goes to the red offal room.
  • Condemned offal goes into the marked condemned bin.
  • Do not remove a cyst or abnormal part yourself.

In the red offal room

  1. Separate the organs: liver (remove the gall bladder carefully so bile does not spill), heart, lungs, kidneys.
  2. Trim off fat, blood vessels and any part the inspector ordered.
  3. Rinse with clean, potable water.
  4. Put on clean trays or hooks, not on the floor.
  5. Chill quickly. Offal spoils faster than carcass meat.
  6. Pack and label as your plant procedure says.

Hygiene

  • Red offal must be kept separate from rough offal at all times. Use different rooms, containers and tools.
  • Wash hands and sterilise knives often.
  • Keep containers clean and covered.

lessons.title: Handling rough offal
lessons.html:
What rough offal is

Rough offal (also called green or white offal) is the stomachs and intestines. Sheep and goats have four stomach compartments: rumen, reticulum, omasum and abomasum. Cleaned stomachs are sold as tripe (for example for mogodu), and some intestines are cleaned for sausage casings or sold as derms.

Rough offal is dirty

The stomachs and intestines are full of chewed grass and dung, which contain many germs. Rough offal must be handled in a separate room, away from carcasses and red offal.

Steps in the rough offal room

  1. Separate the stomachs from the intestines.
  2. Empty the rumen and other stomachs into the correct waste chute. Do not let contents splash onto clean areas.
  3. Wash the stomachs with clean water. Many plants then scald them in hot water to remove the inner lining, and wash again.
  4. Empty and clean the intestines if your plant uses them, or send them to waste.
  5. Chill cleaned tripe quickly and pack as your plant procedure says.

Hygiene and safety

  • Workers in the rough offal room must not go into the clean area without changing and washing.
  • Keep floors clear of stomach contents; they are slippery.
  • Hot water and scalding machines can burn. Use them only if trained.
  • Condemned rough offal goes into the marked bins.

Key points

  • Open the belly with the blade outwards so the guts are not cut.
  • Keep organs matched to the carcass until the inspector has passed them.
  • Red offal: liver, heart, lungs, kidneys, tongue, spleen.
  • Rough offal: stomachs and intestines, handled in a separate room.
  • Never let rough offal, its contents or its workers contaminate the clean area.
  • Chill offal quickly because it spoils fast.
